newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco sees closer metal-profit link.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco sees closer metal-profit link.

text.p: Alumina, aluminium and bauxite miner Comalco Ltd said on Monday its profits would be more sensitive to aluminium prices in 1997 due to an increase in production.
"This year we will produce much more metal, therefore any change in the metal price will have a greater impact on our profit," Comalco chief executive Terry Palmer a news conference.
Comalco earlier reported a net loss of A$16.8 million on a joint venture basis for calendar 1996, compared with a profit of A$232.3 million a year earlier.

Palmer said that every one U.S. cent per pound increase in the price of aluminium would result in an A$11 million increase in 1997 after tax profit. A one cent rise in aluminium prices in 1996 translated to a A$9 million rise in after tax profit, he said.
Palmer also said the company's sensitivity to the Australian dollar would also increase this year.
For every one U.S. cent fall in the value of the Australian dollar, after tax profit would increase by A$9 million, A$2 million more than in calendar 1996.

Comalco said in a statement accompanying its results that an increase in the U.S. dollar average exchange rate to 78 US cents in calendar 1996, from 74 cents in 1995, affected profit adversely by A$35 million.
The Australian dollar was trading around US$0.7765 on Monday.
Comalco said earlier that a 13.4 U.S. cent drop in LME aluminium prices to 69.6 U.S. cents in 1996, together with lower premiums, had accounted for an A$166 million reduction in its operating profit.
Comalco shares were seven cents lower at A$6.75 at 10.40 a.m. (2340 GMT).
